title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Misuse of Market Power) Bill 2014
short_title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Misuse of Market Power) Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would give courts an additional power to order corporations found to have misused market power to reduce their market share or power.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission or another person could seek an order within three years of a contravention, requiring a reduction within two years.
The changes would supplement existing court powers under competition law and would take effect on the day after the bill received Royal Assent.
changes: A new divestiture provision would address breaches of the market power rules.
Courts could make consent orders without finding a contravention if all parties agreed.
Courts could accept a corporation's undertaking instead of issuing an order.
summary.affected: Corporations subject to market power rules, the Commission and people applying for orders are affected.
